grades.reason: Lists exception encodings, not translation-cache invalidation procedures.

grades.quote: _In many implementations, an SFENCE.VMA instruction with rs1=_ `x0` _will therefore either terminate all previously-launched speculative executions of the addresstranslation algorithm (for the specified ASID, if applicable), or simply wait for them to complete (in which case any address-translation cache entries created will be invalidated by the SFENCE.VMA as appropriate).
grades.reason: Explains how SFENCE.VMA invalidates cached translations while preventing speculative translations from preserving stale entries.

grades.quote: As a temporary Cache for the processor to store information about page tables in the operating system, TLB is used to speed up the translation of virtual addresses to physical addresses for fetch and load/store operations in mapped address translation mode.
grades.reason: Provides background on cached page-table translations, but no procedure for invalidating them after changes.

grades.quote: Note that writing `satp` does not imply any ordering constraints between page-table updates and subsequent address translations, nor does it imply any invalidation of address-translation caches. If the new address space’s page tables have been modified, or if an ASID is reused, it may be necessary to execute an SFENCE.VMA instruction (see Section 12.2.1) after, or in some cases before, writing `satp` .
grades.reason: Directly identifies SFENCE.VMA as necessary for consistency after page-table changes and warns that writing satp does not invalidate cached translations.
